2K.9 It is a foolish people who blaspheme God's name.

precepts.text: Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters. Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness. Remember what we read, the dragon fought and his angels. That is what we are reading about here. Christ and Michael fighting against the white man and his army. The heads of leviathan is talking about all the heads. Europe, France, all of them. America, all of them. That dragon, Christ is going to destroy the whole government.
precepts.point: And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him. Who deceived the world is not just a spiritual demon. This is his children. The white man, Edom, Lucifer, that transformed himself into an angel of light.

note.label: Lucifer: The Antichrist

precepts.why:
“Thou didst divide the sea by thy strength: thou brakest the heads of the dragons in the waters.” Remember what we read: “the dragon fought and his angels.” That's what we are reading about here: Christ and Michael and the angels fighting against the white man and his army.

“Thou brakest the heads of leviathan in pieces, and gavest him to be meat to the people inhabiting the wilderness.” The heads of leviathan are all the heads: Europe, France, all of them; America, all of them. Christ is going to destroy that dragon, the whole government.

That is why Revelation says the dragon and his angels “prevailed not; neither was their place found any more in heaven.” They don't win against Michael and the angels. When Christ returns, Michael and the angels fight against the white man and his army, and every head of leviathan is broken in pieces.

precepts.text: Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.
precepts.point: Yet thou shalt be brought down to hell, to the sides of the pit. God said, regardless of all the technological power you have got, you are going to be brought down to hell. America, Babylon, Lucifer.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!” God has not changed the subject from Babylon; he changed the metaphor. Babylon, Lucifer, America: the same thing. America weakens all the nations.

“I will exalt my throne above the stars of God”: that is space travel. “I will sit also upon the mount of the congregation, in the sides of the north”: that is slavery. When you are sitting on somebody, you have conquered them, you beat them. Well, who is the congregation? Is it the church, the Baptist church, the Catholic church?

“Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed; this mount Zion, wherein thou hast dwelt.”

The congregation is the people God purchased of old, the rod of his inheritance, the people he redeemed, mount Zion where he dwelt. That is Israel. So when Lucifer says he will sit upon the mount of the congregation, he is saying he will sit on God’s own inheritance, and that is what was done to us in the sides of the north, North America.

precepts.text: Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name. Primarily the nations, and in some instances our own people.
precepts.point: O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever? How? By making our signs their signs. The whitewashed imagery is blasphemy.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
The psalm ends its first cry with, “O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever?” How does the enemy blaspheme? By making our signs their signs. White Jesus is blasphemy. White angels are blasphemy. All these whitewashed images are blasphemy; it is evil.

Further down Asaph says it again: “Remember this, that the enemy hath reproached, O Lord, and that the foolish people have blasphemed thy name.” The foolish people are the nations, primarily, and in some instances our own people too.

To blaspheme is to speak evil of his name, his reputation. White Jesus is blasphemy. He died for all people, the gospel is for all people, all nations can be saved: blasphemy. He isn't the son of God, he doesn't exist, I'm an atheist, evolution: blasphemy. His name is blasphemed every day all around the world.

That is why the enemy is not only the one who burned the sanctuary and the synagogues, as Babylon and Assyria did. The enemy is also the one who keeps reproaching God's name by painting over his people, so that “We see not our signs.” We don't see statues of David or Solomon or Christ as black men; we see their images, their depictions.

precepts.text: And laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images. They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain, Portugal, Britain, the Dutch, the French. They all did it, and they still do it.
precepts.point: O God, how long shall the adversary reproach? shall the enemy blaspheme thy name for ever? How? By making our signs their signs. The whitewashed imagery is blasphemy.

note.label: Blasphemers & Traitors: Judge Not Before the Time

precepts.why:
The psalm says of the enemy, “they set up their ensigns for signs.” What are their ensigns for signs? Cesare Borgia; Mother Mary, white Mary; baby white Jesus; white prophets; the Last Supper; the Sistine Chapel. Posing themselves as God, as the prophets, as the angels, as the heavenly Father: whitewashing our ensigns and making our ensigns their signs.

Maccabees shows it was done before: they “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The book of the law is our Bible, and the heathen sought to paint the likeness of their own images into it.

They made our signs their signs. The Greeks did it, the Romans did it, Spain did it, Portugal did it, Britain did it, the Dutch, the French: they all did it, and they still do it. It was blasphemy back then, and it is blasphemy now.

That is why Asaph cries, “We see not our signs.” The heathen painted themselves into the book of the law, and our people no longer see their own images in the scriptures that were written about them.

precepts.text: Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people, sealing them as the purchased congregation.
precepts.point: The Most High purchased us when He instituted animal sacrifice, when Moses sprinkled the blood over the people.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks the Most High to “Remember thy congregation, which thou hast purchased of old; the rod of thine inheritance, which thou hast redeemed”. When did he purchase us? When he instituted animal sacrifice, when Moses sprinkled the blood over the people.

“And Moses took half of the blood, and put it in basons; and half of the blood he sprinkled on the altar. And he took the book of the covenant, and read in the audience of the people: and they said, All that the Lord hath said will we do, and be obedient. And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the Lord hath made with you concerning all these words.”

Moses sprinkled the blood of the covenant on the people, sealing them as the purchased congregation. That is the congregation the psalmist is pleading for, the sheep of his pasture, Israel, asking why his anger smokes against them and that he remember Mount Zion where he dwelt.

precepts.text: The heathen sought to paint the likeness of their images in the book of the law, setting up their own patterns.
precepts.point: They said in their hearts, let us destroy them together, and burned up all the synagogues of God in the land.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
“Thine enemies roar in the midst of thy congregations; they set up their ensigns for signs.” The ensigns set up for signs are the other nations setting up their images, histories and laws for us to follow. In school you get American history, French history, all the histories of their people, never ours.

Maccabees shows the heathen doing the same thing to the scriptures themselves. Judas and his men “laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” The heathen sought to paint the likeness of their images in the book of the law, setting up their own patterns in the place of God's.

That is the enemy roaring in the midst of the congregations, breaking down the carved work with axes and hammers, casting fire into the sanctuary and defiling the dwelling place of the Most High's name. They said in their hearts, let us destroy them together, and set their own ensigns where God's should be.

precepts.text: Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation and shall not be ashamed nor confounded, world without end.
precepts.point: We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; He put us in captivity for our disobedience. As long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist prays, “O let not the oppressed return ashamed: let the poor and needy praise thy name.” The congregation of the poor is the Israelites, and Isaiah gives the answer to that prayer: “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.”

Our people will not return to the Lord ashamed. The prophecies show Israel will be redeemed with a mighty salvation, an everlasting salvation, not ashamed nor confounded, world without end. That is the covenant the psalmist asks the Most High to have respect unto: that his people would inherit the Kingdom of Heaven, established from Adam and Shem onward.

We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; he put us in captivity for our disobedience, and the dark places of the earth are full of the habitations of cruelty. But as long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting. Israel shall be saved.

precepts.text: Thy word is very pure, therefore thy servant loveth it, the mark of a pure-hearted reading of the scriptures.
precepts.point: We must keep in mind it is because of our own doing; He put us in captivity for our disobedience. As long as we come with a clean heart and fix what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting.

note.label: Psalm 74: Have Respect Unto the Covenant

precepts.why:
The psalmist asks the Most High to remember how “the foolish man reproacheth thee daily” and to “Forget not the voice of thine enemies: the tumult of those that rise up against thee increaseth continually.” The enemy thinks evil upon their beds every day on how to oppress and crush Israel.

Against that stands the servant of Psalm 119: “Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.” That is the mark of a pure-hearted reading of the scriptures. The foolish man reproaches; the servant loves the word because it is pure.

That is the clean heart we have to come with. He put us in captivity for our disobedience, but as long as we come with a clean heart, loving his pure word and fixing what we must fix, there is no issue for those repenting. Let the poor and needy praise his name.
